records.locator: Jataka XI.23, uploaded physical PDF729 / printed p719
records.source_paraphrase: A weak/debilitated or inimical ruler of the twelfth from the Lagna lord is said to indicate migration abroad. Favorable Venus aspect is claimed to distinguish remaining abroad permanently.
records.source_layer: Classical verse via V. Subramanya Sastri translation, Sanskrit printed adjacent
records.critical_limit: A private travel record may verify migration and settlement separately, but this is not a validated prediction. Exact 12th-from-lagna-lord counting and aspects unresolved.

records.locator: Jataka XI.23, physical PDF729 / printed p719
records.source_paraphrase: The same foreign-residence yoga attributes a small town to solar obscuration of that relevant ruler and a prosperous municipality to its greater strength.
records.critical_limit: Destination category must be operationally defined, opportunity/cohort controlled and not conflated with country of residence.

records.locator: Jataka XI.24, physical PDF729 / printed p719
records.source_paraphrase: A dignified 12th-from-Lagna-lord ruler in kendra/trine surrounded by benefics allegedly indicates agreeable foreign residence; aspect by Jupiter/Moon/Venus intensifies favorable destination, whereas an inimical second-position exception predicts staying in one's own country.
records.source_layer: Classical source verse via Sastri English
records.critical_limit: Competing exceptions are in same verse. Not all travel or pleasurable destinations count as prediction success.

records.locator: Jataka XI.25, physical PDF729–730 / printed pp719–720
records.source_paraphrase: Movable Lagna, movable lagna lord and movable-sign aspects predict fortune abroad; corresponding fixed conditions predict prosperity in native country.
records.source_layer: Classical verse via Sastri and a separate editor note of parallel appearance in an unreadable work title
records.critical_limit: Source has a real directional contrast. Scoring requires frozen sign/lord/aspect and financial definition; parallel-source attribution not independently verified.

records.locator: Jataka XI.61, physical PDF742–743 / printed pp732–733
records.source_paraphrase: Weak second-house lord plus absence of a benefic aspect to Lagna is given as a poverty or wealth-loss prediction.
records.source_layer: Classical source verse via Sastri English
records.critical_limit: Keep inverse cases and person-level socioeconomic opportunity; broad poverty claim not proof.

records.locator: Jataka XI.62, physical PDF743 / printed p733
records.source_paraphrase: Lagna lord in second and second lord in eleventh, or eleventh lord in Lagna, is associated with finding treasure or valuable property.
records.source_layer: Classical translated verse with separate Sastri note recording textual variant
records.critical_limit: Finding unearned treasure differs from gradual wealth, buying property or family inheritance; rare-event prevalence must be penalized.

records.locator: Jataka XI.64, physical PDF743 / printed p733
records.source_paraphrase: Second lord obscured by Sun and simultaneously debilitated and in malefic D60 division is associated with becoming burdened by debt.
records.source_layer: Classical translated verse; Sastri NOTES add another comparable yoga from a separate treatise
records.critical_limit: Debt must be defined by liabilities versus wealth; D60 is strongly time-sensitive and depends on source-specific subdivision boundaries. No financial advice.

records.locator: Jataka XIV.68, physical PDF890 / printed p880
records.source_paraphrase: Four or five planets in ninth in exaltation/own sign or corresponding favorable subdivisions together with ninth lord are assigned exceptional fortune; source differentiates success in native versus foreign country according to exact varga dignity.
records.source_layer: Classical translated verse, original Sanskrit printed adjacent
records.critical_limit: Not generic foreign travel. Four/five-planets-in-ninth signatures can be rare or geometrically constrained, and inherited opportunity heavily affects outcomes.

records.locator: Jataka XVII.82–83, physical PDF1004 / printed p994
records.source_paraphrase: When the relevant sign ruler is in a movable sign or its D9 and the Kālacakra period itself is movable, foreign migration is predicted during that period. Verse 83 says the condition may last while that cakra lasts; when only one of two conditions holds, the interpretation depends on relative strength.
records.source_layer: Classical translated verses plus commentary; page visually checked
records.critical_limit: An explicitly timed prediction requiring frozen Kālacakra Dasha mechanics, sign strength, departure/return dates and separate mixed-condition outcomes. Not an independently verified human result.

methodology.not_new: Existing B20 and B24/B25 covered other fortune, housing and Karakamsha yogas; B41 is restricted to these newly identified XI/XIV/XVII verses.
methodology.sensitive_rules: Historical financial status is not financial advice; do not infer any individual's private debts.
